why_relevant: Montenegrin news portal with an economy stream; adds redundancy so that a personnel story is not missed if a primary outlet is blocked or deletes an item. Also carries regional (Serbian/Bosnian) bank-group news relevant to parent-company reorganisations that cascade into Montenegrin subsidiaries.

source_name: Portal eUprava Crne Gore — vacancy/competition notices
why_relevant: National e-government portal that republishes Uprava za kadrove calls and other official notices. Useful as a secondary/mirror channel and as a discovery surface for institutional publishers not yet in the actor map.

source_name: eUprava Crne Gore — e-government service catalogue (register services)
why_relevant: Catalogues the formal service routes for register extracts (izvod iz CRPS), free-access-to-information requests and financial statement filing — i.e. the legal/manual fallback path when automated register access is blocked.

source_name: eUprava Montenegro - business registration service pages
why_relevant: Explains the registration procedures and the exact legal form names used for foreign presence in Montenegro, which supplies the correct query vocabulary for CRPS lookups and for spotting a vendor's first legal footprint.

source_name: eUprava Crne Gore - service catalogue (Saglasnost na imenovanje izvršnog direktora)
why_relevant: Documents the administrative procedure by which the state grants consent to the appointment of an executive director in state-owned companies, and catalogues services of the Capital Market Authority. Explains WHO must approve an appointment and WHICH body issues the paper trail - useful for knowing where to look for each institution.

High-traffic general classifieds carrying a jobs vertical. Relevant mainly for the agent/retail layer of the payments ecosystem — payment-point operators and cash-in/cash-out agents recruit counter staff here rather than through formal boards, which is a leading indicator of network expansion by the PIs behind them.

Provides comparable asset, market-share and rank figures per Montenegrin bank (e.g. Zapad 5th/+19.16%, Lovćen 7th/+11.65%, Ziraat 11th/1.34%). Not a hiring source, but it is the normaliser that turns raw vacancy counts from the corporate channels into growth-adjusted signal and tells the analyst which small bank's three openings actually matter.

Montenegrin news portal with a standing economy rubric. Secondary breadth source for appointment notices and corporate reorganisation items; useful for catching stories that only get PR-wire distribution.

source_name: Coreit d.o.o. Podgorica - Montenegrin systems integrator (company profile via EMIS)
why_relevant: Coreit is a Podgorica consulting/system-integration firm that states it runs IT projects for financial institutions; profile pages of this kind give key executives and financials, which is how you detect leadership change and growth at private integrators that publish little themselves.

Aggregator with per-employer pages for Montenegrin financial-supervision bodies (confirmed page for Agencija za nadzor osiguranja), giving a low-friction hiring feed for supervisors whose own sites publish irregularly.

source_name: Posao.crna.gora.me — job ads plus business directory (Poslovni adresar)
why_relevant: Dual-purpose: a vacancy feed and a Montenegrin business directory ('Poslovni adresar') indexed by city. The directory half helps resolve PI addresses, branch presence and sibling entities, supporting actor-map maintenance as much as hiring capture.

International staffing group active in the Adriatic region including Montenegro. Multinational agencies typically hold the mandates for regional bank shared-service and IT build-outs; their posted roles reveal where a group is placing capacity before any corporate announcement.

Politically aligned Montenegrin portal. Low credibility for facts, but it reports dismissal and patronage allegations about state-linked financial institutions that mainstream outlets sit on. Value is as a tripwire only — every claim needs corroboration before it enters the intelligence record.
Sells per-company reports built on Dun & Bradstreet plus local sources, including directors and shareholders — a paid corroboration route for a specific entity when register access fails.
Covers the state of the general collective agreement and worker rights disputes; a secondary outlet that sometimes carries union positions the mainstream skips.

source_name: MarketScreener – company/board profiles for Montenegrin subsidiaries and parents
why_relevant: Third-party aggregator maintaining structured board/manager lists for NLB Banka a.d. Podgorica (MEMONBRA1PG2) and the parent groups; useful for change-detection and for resolving officer names/roles when primary sites are stale.

source_name: Mojazarada.me – Zakon o radu / sindikat explainer
why_relevant: Montenegrin worker-facing explainer of union rights, representativeness thresholds and strike rules in local language — useful for the cell glossary and for judging when a bank union becomes a legally recognised bargaining counterparty.

source_name: OTP Bank – Montenegro market page (group Global Securities Services / country page)
why_relevant: Group-maintained English country page describing the Montenegrin operation; useful for baseline entity facts, official English naming of CKB, and occasional structural updates.

entity_name: Regional card-personalisation bureaux serving ME banks
source_name: Regional card-personalisation bureaux serving ME banks (Zeta, SIS, Cards Print - RS-based)
why_relevant: No Montenegrin card-personalisation bureau surfaced; the function appears to be served from Serbia/region or in-house at banks. These vendors' service pages (including in-house personalisation leasing models) are the practical place where a Montenegrin bank customer or a new local engagement would appear.
Second-tier people aggregator; useful triangulation when ZoomInfo and LinkedIn disagree on a person's current employer, and it indexes some smaller Balkan financial entities.

Podgorica city portal. Same rationale as Gradska.me but for the capital, where most bank head offices and the largest branch networks sit; picks up head-office relocations, office openings/closures and local hiring drives.
